papers.title: Uncertainty Quantification in Control Problems for Flocking Models
papers.abstract: In this paper the optimal control of flocking models with random inputs is investigated from a numerical point of view. The effect of uncertainty in the interaction parameters is studied for a Cucker-Smale type model using a generalized polynomial chaos (gPC) approach. Numerical evidence of threshold effects in the alignment dynamic due to the random parameters is given. The use of a selective model predictive control permits to steer the system towards the desired state even in unstable regimes.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate threshold effects in alignment dynamics due to random interaction parameters in flocking models.
summary_en.method: A generalized polynomial chaos approach combined with selective model predictive control is employed to manage uncertainty.
summary_en.result: The system can be steered towards the desired state even in unstable regimes.
summary_en.validation: Numerical simulations verify the effectiveness of the proposed control under random parameters.
